confidence_note: DB title 'Bağımlılık Çağı'; the book is Chasing the Scream. Rat Park (Bruce Alexander, Simon Fraser University, 1970s) and the Vietnam heroin follow-up are in Hari's book per Wikipedia and summaries; exact percentages and cage details were not verified, so none are used beyond 'about one in five' (hedged) and 'most'. Replications of Rat Park have been mixed and critics fault Hari's rigor; story carries a one-line caveat.
facts: Bruce Alexander, a psychologist in Canada, questioned the standard experiment in which a rat alone in a bare cage chooses between water and water laced with a drug.
In the standard setup the isolated rat keeps going back to the drug, which was taken as proof the drug itself hooks.
Alexander asked whether the cage was the cause and built Rat Park: a large space with other rats, toys and room to move.
Hari reports that the rats in the park drank far less of the drug solution than the isolated rats.
Hari pairs it with American soldiers in Vietnam: a large share used heroin there (about one in five) yet most stopped after coming home.
Hari's reading: addiction is shaped by environment and connection, not only by chemistry.
Caveat: later attempts to repeat Rat Park gave mixed results; it is an argument, not settled proof.
scene_details: Two bottles in a bare cage
A park with toys and other rats
tension: The same drug on offer, but the rats that had a life barely touched it.
opening_idea: Open on the lone rat and the two bottles.

lessons.idea: When someone keeps returning to a habit, look at the cage as well as the habit.
lessons.anchor: Rat Park's rats drank far less.
lessons.everyday_example_idea: A colleague who scrolls through lunch alone.

reflect_final: Which habit of yours gets stronger when you are lonely or bored, and what in your week could change that, rather than your willpower?

use_cases.situation: A friend is struggling with a habit.
use_cases.move: Ask what their days look like before asking what they will quit.

use_cases.situation: You want to cut a habit.
use_cases.move: Change one thing around it, such as who you are with when it happens.

use_cases.situation: Talk at home about a teenager's screen time.
use_cases.move: Offer time together instead of a rule alone.

pocket_idea: Two bottles, one bare cage: ask what is missing from a person's days before asking what they cannot resist.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: The rats that had a park barely touched the drug the lonely rats kept returning to.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Alexander's Rat Park: the lone rats drank the drug, the rats in the big cage with company mostly did not; Vietnam soldiers stopped at home.
